# Settings

37 settings, by section (the Settings page's tabs) then name. Change one with `:set NAME=VALUE`, `settings set NAME VALUE` or the Settings page; the values live in settings.json.

## General

<a id="setting-dim-unfocused"></a>
### `dim-unfocused`

integer · default `20` · section General · declared by ochazuke

Percent a list without the focus fades toward the background; its selected row stays marked (0 is off)

<a id="setting-focus-display"></a>
### `focus-display`

string · default `off` · choices `off`, `noun`, `stack` · section General · declared by ochazuke

Show where the focus is beside the mode: off, noun (the focused noun) or stack (the focus path, outermost first)

<a id="setting-history-fetches"></a>
### `history-fetches`

boolean · default `false` · section General · declared by ochazuke

Keep data requests (fetches) in the history file too

<a id="setting-history-limit"></a>
### `history-limit`

integer · default `500` · section General · declared by ochazuke

Action history entries kept across restarts (0 keeps none)

<a id="setting-modal-dim"></a>
### `modal-dim`

integer · default `35` · section General · declared by ochazuke

Percent the page behind a modal fades toward the background (0 is off)

<a id="setting-sequence-inherit"></a>
### `sequence-inherit`

string · default `drop` · choices `drop`, `keep` · section General · declared by ochazuke

A key sequence a mode inherits from the mode it extends (a row's normal d d in visual-line) when the mode binds the keys typed on its own (visual-line d): drop runs the mode's own key at once, as in Vim (V j d); keep waits for the inherited sequence

<a id="setting-sequence-timeout"></a>
### `sequence-timeout`

duration · default `0s` · section General · declared by ochazuke

How long a pending key sequence (g g, z R, the terminal leader) waits for its next key before the shorter binding runs; 0 waits until a key comes

<a id="setting-sequence-unknown"></a>
### `sequence-unknown`

string · default `pass` · choices `pass`, `swallow` · section General · declared by ochazuke

A key no binding continues a pending sequence with: pass ends the sequence (its shorter binding runs) and handles the key as if typed alone; swallow drops the sequence and the key with a notice

<a id="setting-theme"></a>
### `theme`

string · default `adaptive` · choices `adaptive`, `dark`, `light`, `mono` · section General · declared by ochazuke

Colour scheme (themes.json adds more)

## aliases

<a id="setting-aliases.shadow"></a>
### `aliases.shadow`

string · default `refuse` · choices `refuse`, `allow` · section aliases · declared by ochazuke

A bare actions.json alias (w!, q) named like a verb: refuse skips the row and reports it; allow loads it, and typed alone it runs the alias, the verb still reached as noun verb

## chooser

<a id="setting-chooser.enter"></a>
### `chooser.enter`

string · default `open` · choices `open`, `pick` · section chooser · declared by ochazuke

Enter on a chooser row that can be both opened and picked (a folder in a folder chooser): open browses into it (alt+enter picks it), pick takes it (ctrl+l opens it)

<a id="setting-chooser.remember-source"></a>
### `chooser.remember-source`

boolean · default `true` · section chooser · declared by ochazuke

A chooser with several sources (tab cycles them) reopens on the source last used for its kind; off opens on its first source

## docs

<a id="setting-docs.show-config"></a>
### `docs.show-config`

boolean · default `true` · section docs · declared by ochazuke

The docs viewer (docs open, :help) marks where your settings.json and bindings.json differ from the defaults with yours: lines; off, a page reads as the committed reference

## forms

<a id="setting-forms.single-path"></a>
### `forms.single-path`

string · default `chooser` · choices `chooser`, `alone`, `form` · section forms · declared by ochazuke

A key or command line whose only missing required argument is a path: chooser opens the path chooser at once and its pick runs the action (optional arguments left out); alone does so only when the path is its one argument; form opens the args form (on the path, its chooser open over it)

## help

<a id="setting-help.pending-modes"></a>
### `help.pending-modes`

boolean · default `false` · section help · declared by ochazuke

The ? help's pick and table views offer the pending modes too (counts, operators, the terminal leader, key-sequence prefixes)

<a id="setting-help.pick-view"></a>
### `help.pick-view`

boolean · default `true` · section help · declared by ochazuke

S in the ? help shows the keys for a noun and mode you pick

<a id="setting-help.table-view"></a>
### `help.table-view`

boolean · default `true` · section help · declared by ochazuke

S in the ? help shows a noun's keys as a table, a column per mode

## markdown

<a id="setting-markdown.note-author"></a>
### `markdown.note-author`

string · default `owner` · section markdown · declared by ochazuke

The author a new note in a Markdown document is signed with

## pages

<a id="setting-pages.hidden"></a>
### `pages.hidden`

list · default `[]` · section pages · declared by ochazuke

Page ids left out of the tabs and ctrl+j/k (page.hide and page.show write it); page.open still opens them

## palette

<a id="setting-palette.missing-opens-form"></a>
### `palette.missing-opens-form`

boolean · default `true` · section palette · declared by ochazuke

Enter on a command line, or a key, whose action lacks a required argument opens a form for its arguments; off names the missing word instead

## path

<a id="setting-path.field"></a>
### `path.field`

string · default `picker` · choices `picker`, `text` · section path · declared by ochazuke

A path field in a form: picker (a stop whose enter, space or i opens the path chooser) or text (typed freely; enter in normal mode or ctrl+space opens the path chooser)

<a id="setting-path.hidden"></a>
### `path.hidden`

boolean · default `false` · section path · declared by ochazuke

The path chooser's browse source lists hidden entries (names starting with .); off, typing a path starting with . still lists them

<a id="setting-path.no-auto-list"></a>
### `path.no-auto-list`

list · default `["/Volumes/","/mnt/","/media/","/run/media/"]` · section path · declared by ochazuke

Folders under these prefixes (external volumes) are never listed on their own: browse waits until you open one or type a path into it

<a id="setting-path.start"></a>
### `path.start`

string · default `base` · choices `base`, `home`, `cwd` · section path · declared by ochazuke

Where the path chooser's browse starts when the parameter names no base and the field is empty: base (the folder the application gives, such as the open file's, else the working directory), home or cwd

## rename

<a id="setting-rename.select"></a>
### `rename.select`

boolean · default `true` · section rename · declared by ochazuke

A rename opens with the whole name selected: typing replaces it, a motion keeps it and moves; off opens it with the cursor at the end

## repeat

<a id="setting-repeat.empty"></a>
### `repeat.empty`

string · default `info` · choices `info`, `silent` · section repeat · declared by ochazuke

Dot-repeat (.) with nothing to repeat here: info says nothing to repeat on the status line, plain; silent shows nothing

## settings

<a id="setting-settings.autosave"></a>
### `settings.autosave`

boolean · default `false` · section settings · declared by ochazuke

A session write (a :set line, setting verbs with session scope) goes straight to settings.json; off keeps it for this session until settings.write (alias save, mksettings). The Settings page and settings set always save at once

<a id="setting-settings.mark-session"></a>
### `settings.mark-session`

boolean · default `true` · section settings · declared by ochazuke

The Settings page draws a session value bold with the saved value beside it, stack  (saved: tabs), while the two differ

## status

<a id="setting-status.segment-order"></a>
### `status.segment-order`

list · default `[]` · section status · declared by ochazuke

Segment ids in the order the header rule draws them (segment.move writes it); the rest follow

<a id="setting-status.segments"></a>
### `status.segments`

boolean · default `true` · section status · declared by ochazuke

Show the status segments (cpu, disk, an extension's) in the header rule; off hides them all and stops their refreshes

## tones

<a id="setting-tones.selected-background"></a>
### `tones.selected-background`

string · default `drop` · choices `drop`, `keep` · section tones · declared by ochazuke

A cell drawn on a tone background (an error) on the selected row: drop keeps the row one reverse bar; keep draws the cell on its background, bold, out of the bar

## tree

<a id="setting-tree.breadcrumb"></a>
### `tree.breadcrumb`

string · default `line` · choices `line`, `title`, `off` · section tree · declared by ochazuke

Where a zoomed tree shows the levels it hides: line (a dimmed line above its rows), title (in the header beside the mode, while the tree has the focus) or off

<a id="setting-tree.zoom"></a>
### `tree.zoom`

string · default `manual` · choices `manual`, `auto`, `off` · section tree · declared by ochazuke

Tree zoom: manual (only z +, z -, z 0 and h past the top), auto (also zooms when the selected row's indent takes over half the tree's width) or off (no zoom)

## tree.breadcrumb

<a id="setting-tree.breadcrumb.ancestors"></a>
### `tree.breadcrumb.ancestors`

integer · default `2` · section tree.breadcrumb · declared by ochazuke

How many of the nearest hidden ancestors a zoomed tree's breadcrumb names; farther ones fold into …; 0 names them all

## tree.zoom

<a id="setting-tree.zoom.root"></a>
### `tree.zoom.root`

string · default `crumb` · choices `crumb`, `row` · section tree.zoom · declared by ochazuke

Where a tree's zoomed-on node goes: crumb (it ends the breadcrumb and its children are the top rows) or row (it stays as the top row)

## visual

<a id="setting-visual.after-action"></a>
### `visual.after-action`

string · default `end` · choices `end`, `keep` · section visual · declared by ochazuke

After a key acts on a visual selection of list rows (V j d): end leaves the selection and visual-line, as in Vim; keep keeps the selection on the rows still shown, so the next key acts on them too

<a id="setting-visual.list"></a>
### `visual.list`

string · default `mode` · choices `mode`, `marks` · section visual · declared by ochazuke

V on a list, table or tree: mode enters visual-line, where single keys act on the selection (d, y, an application's own); marks selects in normal mode, as before, the rows' normal keys acting on the selection
